headline: Wild activate Jared Spurgeon off injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Wild have activated defenseman Jared Spurgeon off injured reserve and assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to the AHL's Iowa Wild. Spurgeon was on the ice for practice the day before, as Heather Rule of NHL.com posted.

The timing suits Minnesota, who sit at 12-3-4 with 28 points. Spurgeon has played 10 games so far this season and averages 20.54 minutes, a top-pair workload. At 5-on-5, the Wild generated 67 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) while he was on the ice, and the team's share of expected goals is about 17 percentage points better with him in the lineup. That is a small sample, but it fits the defender who played 79 games last season. For a team whose results have leaned heavily on goaltending (11.4 goals saved above expected), getting a puck-moving defender back is useful. Pitlick, by contrast, was a 7.64-minute depth forward with no points in 12 games and a 53 percent expected goals share, so his departure changes little on the ice.
